prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1349; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a traffic signal on a League City, Texas roadway when the vehicle behind, operated by Driver 2, struck the rear bumper. Passenger, seated in the front passenger position of Driver 1's vehicle, reported immediate pain in the neck and lower back following the impact. The force of the collision appears consistent with the injuries described, and the damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle matches the impact as reported at the scene. Officers observed no prior damage to the vehicle that would suggest an earlier incident. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the applicable policy. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the collision, though no independent witnesses were located to provide a separate account. Both officers on scene and the drivers involved confirmed that Passenger was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Passenger was evaluated at the scene and transported for further medical care. No citations were issued at the time of this report, and the investigation remains open pending additional statements.
